summary: Fix undeclared bundling and leakage by splitting the executor control-flow edit and removing specific task IDs from predictions.

edits.hypothesis: Injecting a domain-agnostic instruction when a tool failure is detected forces the agent to re-examine original inputs rather than relying on generalist model consensus that may miss subtle details due to lack of high-resolution evidence.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt edits alone are static; this mechanism activates conditionally based on actual runtime tool failure events observed in the trajectory, providing dynamic context that static prompts cannot.
edits.trigger_condition: Any tool call in the current step returns a failure status (detected via tool_failure_reason).
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In tasks where roi_crop failed (e.g., q000001), the new next_prompt instructs the agent to ignore the lack of crop evidence and inspect original pixels directly, likely overriding negative llava_med_qa results. (preservative) Success cases like q000003 do not trigger tool failures, so the mechanism remains inactive. (transfer) Generalizes to any task where a specialized inspection tool fails.
edits.mechanism: Injecting a domain-agnostic instruction when a tool failure is detected forces the agent to re-examine original inputs rather than relying on generalist model consensus that may miss subtle details due to lack of high-resolution evidence.

edits.hypothesis: Refining the failure recovery prompt to explicitly mention 'original image pixels' reinforces the visual grounding requirement without introducing task-specific leakage or hardcoded entities.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: The control flow injects the prompt, but the content of the prompt itself must be precise to avoid ambiguity. This edit ensures the language is robust and generalizable.
edits.trigger_condition: Always active as part of the harness definition, but only utilized when has_tool_failure is true in executor.py.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Clarifies the instruction for all tool-failure cases, ensuring the agent knows exactly what to re-examine. (preservative) Does not affect successful tool executions. (transfer) Applicable to any domain where tool failure requires fallback to raw input inspection.
